newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moody's assigns Tri Polyta Finance notes B1.
newsitem.headline: Moody's assigns Tri Polyta Finance notes B1.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on late on Tuesday that it assigned a B1 rating to the proposed US$175 million guaranteed secured notes due 2002 of PT. Tri Polyta International Finance Co B.V. of Indonesia. The notes are guaranteed by Indonesian chemcial company PT. Tri Polyta Indonesia Tbk (TPI).

Positive factors supporting the B1 rating include TPI's position as the largest polypropelene producer in Indonesia, a competitive position that beneifts from tariff protection and expansion goals that mesh with the government's objectives to grow Indonesia's industrial base and expand its petrochemical sector, the rating agency said.

Limting factors include a small revenue base, a narrow product slate, a significant level of margin volatiliy attributed to the cyclicality of its products and raw materials and an aggressive investment schedule that Moody's thinks is likely to use up much of the medium term cash flow.

The rating outlook is positive as completion of the expansion activities is likely to improve the credit profile. The outlook for polypropelene polymer demand growth is high in Indonesia, driven by the rising per capita consumption of the chemical from its current very low level, Moody's said.

TPI's compeittive position and product pricing benefit from tariff protection, but this benefit is partially offset by tariffs on its key feedstock, propylene, which it sources on the global spot market and under a long term propylene supply contract whose pricing structure incorporates a premium above the market price, the rating agency said.
